gloss: to mince, to chop; to carve, to engrave

definitions.explanation: To cut food into small pieces.
To cut or etch a design, pattern, or letters into a hard surface.
For time to pass moment by moment.

examples.japanese: {玉|たま}ねぎを{細|こま}かく{刻|きざ}む。
{木|き}に{名前|なまえ}を{刻|きざ}んだ。
examples.english: I carved my name into the tree.

examples.japanese: {時計|とけい}が{時|とき}を{刻|きざ}んでいる。
examples.english: The clock is ticking away the time.

examples.japanese: ニンジンを{細|ほそ}く{刻|きざ}む。
examples.english: Chop the carrot into thin pieces.

examples.japanese: {刻|きざ}んだネギを{味噌汁|みそしる}に{入|い}れる。
examples.english: Put chopped green onion into the miso soup.

examples.japanese: {石碑|せきひ}に{名前|なまえ}が{刻|きざ}まれている。
examples.english: Names are engraved on the stone monument.

examples.japanese: この{言葉|ことば}を{心|こころ}に{刻|きざ}んでおきたい。
examples.english: I want to engrave these words in my heart.

examples.japanese: {秒針|びょうしん}が{静|しず}かに{時|とき}を{刻|きざ}んでいる。
examples.english: The second hand is quietly ticking away the time.

examples.japanese: {新|あたら}しい{歴史|れきし}を{刻|きざ}む{瞬間|しゅんかん}だった。
examples.english: It was a moment that carved a new page in history.

notes:
{刻|きざ}む has two main meanings: cutting food finely, and carving/engraving.

TRANSITIVITY:
- Type: Transitive ({他動詞|たどうし})
- Pattern: Xを{刻|きざ}む

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {細|こま}かく{刻|きざ}む (to chop finely)
- {時|とき}を{刻|きざ}む (to tick away time)
- {心|こころ}に{刻|きざ}む (to engrave in one's heart, to remember deeply)
- {歴史|れきし}に{刻|きざ}む (to be recorded in history)

COOKING VOCABULARY:
- {刻|きざ}み{ネギ|ねぎ} (chopped green onion)
- {刻|きざ}み{海苔|のり} (shredded nori seaweed)
- みじん{切|ぎ}り (dicing, similar to {刻|きざ}む)
